title: Laredo Woman Indicted on Federal Charges in Fatal Fentanyl Case; Faces Up to Life in Prison
excerpt: A federal grand jury has returned a two-count indictment against a 33-year-old Laredo resident accused of distributing fentanyl that resulted in a person's deat
content:
A federal grand jury has returned a two-count indictment against a 33-year-old Laredo resident accused of distributing fentanyl that resulted in a person's death, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Texas.

Amanda Angelina Sanchez is charged with distribution of fentanyl resulting in death and possession with intent to distribute fentanyl. According to the indictment, Sanchez allegedly distributed fentanyl to another person on March 2, 2025, and that person later died after using the drug.

Sanchez was indicted Nov. 10, pleaded not guilty Nov. 16, and waived her detention hearing on Friday, Nov. 20, according to KGNS and the Laredo Morning Times. She remains in federal custody, and her final pretrial conference is set for Jan. 5 before U.S. District Judge Marina Garcia Marmolejo.

If convicted on the death-linked charge, Sanchez faces at least 20 years and up to life in federal prison, as well as a maximum fine of $1 million.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Leslie Cortez is prosecuting the case, which is part of the Homeland Security Task Force initiative.

An indictment is a formal accusation of criminal conduct, not evidence. A defendant is presumed innocent unless convicted through due process of law.

Sources: U.S. Attorney's Office, Southern District of Texas; KGNS, Nov. 23, 2026; Laredo Morning Times, Nov. 23, 2026.
